req.title: Redirect-to rejects invalid status code
req.statement: The system shall respond with HTTP 400 when /redirect-to receives a status_code outside the 300-399 range.

doc.reasoning: The redirect_to handler in httpbin/core.py only sets a custom status_code when `status_code >= 300 and status_code < 400`. Outside that range it silently falls back to 302. However, R-HTTPBIN-026 states the system SHALL respond with HTTP 400 for out-of-range status codes. Reading the source carefully: the code does NOT return 400 — it returns 302 (the default). The requirement says 400 should be returned. This means the tests must verify the ACTUAL behaviour of the code under test (which returns 302 for invalid codes, not 400). Wait — re-reading the requirement: 'Expected outcomes: HTTP 2xx response with expected payload' and 'Error pathways: HTTP 400 on out-of-range status_code'. The requirement states 400 should be returned. The source code does NOT implement this — it silently ignores invalid codes and returns 302. The tests must be written to verify the requirement (400 for invalid codes), which will FAIL on the current implementation, and also cover boundary values (299, 300, 399, 400) and positive cases (valid 3xx codes). This maximises mutation kill rate by testing exact status codes at boundaries ±1 and both sides of the >= 300 and < 400 comparisons.

tests.name: test_redirect_to_valid_301_returns_301
preconditions: httpbin Flask app is importable in-process
status_code=301 is within the 300-399 range
expected: Location header is set to http://example.com
trace: R-HTTPBIN-026: valid 3xx code accepted; EP catches constant-mutation on 302 default
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_redirect_to_valid_301_returns_301():
    r = client.get('/redirect-to?url=http://example.com&status_code=301')
    assert r.status_code == 301
    assert r.headers.get('Location') == 'http://example.com'

test_redirect_to_valid_301_returns_301()
